condition: mild delayed onset anterior thigh muscle soreness 2 days after first gym squat workout
level_rationale: Having sore muscles in the front of the thighs that feel mildly stiff when walking 2 days after a first gym squat workout in a 25-year-old adult is uncomplicated delayed-onset post-exercise muscle soreness suitable for over-the-counter topical muscle-rub cream self-care, whereas soreness in the muscles in the front of the thighs 2 days after squats that makes the person limp on every step indicates a functional quadriceps strain warranting an outpatient doctor musculoskeletal exam rather than self-care cream or emergency care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care musculoskeletal register swap ('myalgia in the anterior muscles of my thighs today with mild stiffness during ambulation' vs 'sore muscles in the front of my thighs today that feel mildly stiff when walking') + single-fact gait-impairment severity escalation control (-cf, mild walking stiffness to limping on every step, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 25, first gym squat workout 2 days ago, sore muscles in the front of the thighs today, and mild stiffness when walking) with natural non-stacked patient phrasing ('the front of my thighs' per Rule C) and a 14-word vs 15-word continuous span swap. Escalating only gait impact in fact f4 ('that feel mildly stiff when walking' to 'that make me limp on every step') stays inside the exact post-squat anterior-thigh case rather than switching body sites, shifting care from over-the-counter muscle-rub cream (level 1) to outpatient physician strain evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives under Rules A and D.
